an6.14:2.1: This discourse has the same theme as the short teaching attributed to “the seer Rāmaputta” in Isibhāsiyam, a Jain work that gathers various sayings of sages including Hindu and Buddhist. He is evidently the same as the Uddaka Rāmaputta who was the Buddha’s former teacher. In Pali, there are sayings attributed to him at [sn35.103]() and [dn29:16.13](). Isibhāsiyam 23 is distinctly Sutta-like in vocabulary and idiom. It starts with, “There are two kinds of death in the world, namely a happy death and an unhappy death …”. The exposition laments the suffering of boils, bonds, bars, etc.and determines not to return to transmigration in the future course.
